data.question_title: In how many ways \(n\) books can be arranged in a row so that two specified books are not together?
data.explanation_txt:
Total number of arrangements of \(n\) books in a row \( = n! \)

Number of arrangements in which two specified books come together \( = 2! \times (n-1)! \)

[Assuming the stack of two books to be 1 and the inter-arrangement of books in the stack is \(2!\) ]

So, required number of ways \( = n! - 2(n-1)! = n(n-1)! - 2(n-1)! = (n-2)(n-1)! \)

data.question_title:
In my village a fair is held every year. If I happen to be in my village on the day of the fair, I make it a point to attend it. I attend it this year and I retain very happy impressions of all the sights and sounds that I enjoyed.

It was a cloudy day and so I went to the fair on foot. On the way I saw a number of villagers, dressed in their best clothes, going to the fair. They appeared to be in high spirits. They were accompanied by their children who wore turbans of dark red colour. As I approached the fair, I heard a mingling noise. A number of booths and stalls constituting the bazaars of the fair met my eyes. Every villager was buying sweets. The children seemed to be going crazy about sweets.

In the midst of a vast crowd I saw a rope-dancer amusing the audience by keeping his balance wonderfully on the rope. The villagers clapped their hands. A little further I saw the inevitable juggler. He was accompanied by two children; one of whom played on the flute, while the other beat a small drum. The juggler was holding the villagers spell bound by his tricks. The simple minded villagers looked at him with open mouthed wonder and went almost delirious with joy at every new trick.
